LESSON: PRESERVATION AND STORAGE OF CEREALS AND PULSES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Preservation and storage of cereals and pulses
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Preservation and storage of cereals and pulses, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How does preservation and storage of cereals and pulses enhance food security?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Preservation and storage of cereals and pulses together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: The learner displays unity by working collaboratively with others to preserve and store cereals and pulses.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Food security: The learner gains knowledge and skills on preserving foods.

Link to other subjects:

Social studies: The learner listens to/observes a resource person who narrates to them the traditional methods of preserving and storing

cereals and pulses.

Suggested learning resources:

• Ashes.

• Containers with fitting lids.

• Clean sack or mats.

• Hermetic bags.

• Digital devices.

• Print and non print media.
